00001| /**
00002|  * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
00003|  *
00004|  * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
00005|  * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
00006|  * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
00007|  * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
00008|  * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
00009|  *
00010|  * Dual mode:
00011|  *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
00012|  *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
00013|  *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
00014|  *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
00015|  *
00016|  * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
00017|  * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
00018|  */
00019| 
00020| import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
00021| import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
00022| import { dirname } from 'node:path';
00023| import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.
00041|  *
00042|  * @param {{prompt:string, modelPolicy?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00043|  * @returns {string[]}
00044|  */
00045| export function buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input) {
00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');
00052|   }
00053|   return cliArgs;
00054| }
00055| 
00056| /**
00057|  * Report the observed model in the caller's namespace.
00058|  *
00059|  * When the host prefixed the requested model with `vercel/` (extra.cliModel !==
00060|  * input.model), OpenCode observes it back in its own provider namespace —
00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
00062|  * Un-apply exactly that translation so observed === requested holds for callers
00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as
00064|  * a clean gateway id (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4`, not `vercel/anthropic/...`).
00065|  *
00066|  * Everything else passes through untouched: native-default runs (no override —
00067|  * consumers already treat `vercel/google/gemini-3-pro-preview` as canonical),
00068|  * callers that already speak OpenCode's namespace (`vercel/...` requested), and

00072|  * @param {{model?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00073|  * @returns {string|undefined}

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00006|  * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
00007|  * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
00008|  * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
00009|  *
00010|  * Dual mode:
00011|  *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
00012|  *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
00013|  *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
00014|  *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
00015|  *
00016|  * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
00017|  * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
00018|  */
00019| 
00020| import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
00021| import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
00022| import { dirname } from 'node:path';
00023| import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.
00041|  *
00042|  * @param {{prompt:string, modelPolicy?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00043|  * @returns {string[]}
00044|  */
00045| export function buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input) {
00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');
00052|   }
00053|   return cliArgs;
00054| }
00055| 
00056| /**
00057|  * Report the observed model in the caller's namespace.
00058|  *
00059|  * When the host prefixed the requested model with `vercel/` (extra.cliModel !==
00060|  * input.model), OpenCode observes it back in its own provider namespace —
00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
00062|  * Un-apply exactly that translation so observed === requested holds for callers
00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as
00064|  * a clean gateway id (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4`, not `vercel/anthropic/...`).
00065|  *
00066|  * Everything else passes through untouched: native-default runs (no override —
00067|  * consumers already treat `vercel/google/gemini-3-pro-preview` as canonical),
00068|  * callers that already speak OpenCode's namespace (`vercel/...` requested), and
00069|  * extraProviders runs (their providerID isn't `vercel`).
00070|  *
00071|  * @param {string|undefined} observedModel
00072|  * @param {{model?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00073|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00074|  */
00075| export function normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) {
00076|   if (!observedModel) {
00077|     return observedModel;
00078|   }
00079|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00080|   const hostPrefixed = typeof cliModel === 'string' && cliModel !== input.model;
00081|   if (hostPrefixed && observedModel.startsWith('vercel/')) {
00082|     return observedModel.slice('vercel/'.length);
00083|   }
00084|   return observedModel;
00085| }
00086| 
00087| /**
00088|  * Extract transcript from OpenCode JSON output.
00089|  * When run with --format json, OpenCode outputs JSON events to stdout.
00090|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00091|  *
00092|  * @param {string|undefined|null} output
00093|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00094|  */
00095| export function extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) {
00096|   if (!output || !output.trim()) {
00097|     return undefined;
00098|   }
00099| 
00100|   // The --format json output contains JSON events, one per line.
00101|   // Filter to only include lines that look like JSON objects.
00102|   const lines = output.split('\n').filter((line) => {
00103|     const trimmed = line.trim();
00104|     return trimmed.startsWith('{') && trimmed.endsWith('}');
00105|   });
00106| 
00107|   if (lines.length === 0) {
00108|     return undefined;
00109|   }
00110| 
00111|   return lines.join('\n');
00112| }
00113| 
00114| /**
00115|  * Scrape the OpenCode printed logs for the primary build model.
00116|  * Works on OpenCode <= 1.16.x, whose INFO log lines carry providerID/modelID.
00117|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00118|  *
00119|  * @param {string} output
00120|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00121|  */
00122| export function extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output) {
00123|   let observedModel;
00124| 
00125|   for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
00126|     if (!line.includes('service=llm') || !line.includes('small=false') || !line.includes('agent=build')) {
00127|       continue;
00128|     }
00129| 
00130|     const providerMatch = line.match(/providerID=([^\s]+)/);
00131|     const modelMatch = line.match(/modelID=([^\s]+)/);
00132|     const providerID = providerMatch?.[1];
00133|     const modelID = modelMatch?.[1];
00134|     if (providerID && modelID) {
00135|       observedModel = `${providerID}/${modelID}`;
00136|     }
00137|   }
00138| 
00139|   return observedModel;
00140| }
00141| 
00142| /**
00143|  * Extract the session id from the `--format json` event stream.
00144|  * Every emitted event carries a `sessionID` field.
00145|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00146|  *
00147|  * @param {string|undefined} transcript
00148|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00149|  */
00150| export function extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript) {
00151|   if (!transcript) {
00152|     return undefined;
00153|   }
00154| 
00155|   for (const line of transcript.split('\n')) {
00156|     try {
00157|       const event = JSON.parse(line);
00158|       if (typeof event.sessionID === 'string' && event.sessionID) {
00159|         return event.sessionID;
00160|       }
00161|     } catch {
00162|       // Skip non-JSON lines
00163|     }
00164|   }
00165| 
00166|   return undefined;
00167| }
00168| 
00169| /**
00170|  * Extract the observed model from `opencode export <sessionID>` output.
00171|  * Assistant messages carry `providerID` and `modelID` in their info.
00172|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00173|  *
00174|  * @param {string} exportOutput
00175|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00176|  */
00177| export function extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportOutput) {
00178|   const start = exportOutput.indexOf('{');
00179|   if (start === -1) {
00180|     return undefined;
00181|   }
00182| 
00183|   let parsed;
00184|   try {
00185|     parsed = JSON.parse(exportOutput.slice(start));
00186|   } catch {
00187|     return undefined;
00188|   }
00189| 
00190|   const messages = parsed.messages;
00191|   if (!Array.isArray(messages)) {
00192|     return undefined;
00193|   }
00194| 
00195|   for (const message of messages) {
00196|     const info = message.info;
00197|     if (info?.role !== 'assistant') {
00198|       continue;
00199|     }
00200|     if (
00201|       typeof info.providerID === 'string' && info.providerID &&
00202|       typeof info.modelID === 'string' && info.modelID
00203|     ) {
00204|       return `${info.providerID}/${info.modelID}`;
00205|     }
00206|   }
00207| 
00208|   return undefined;
00209| }
00210| 
00211| /**
00212|  * Run OpenCode over the workspace at `input.cwd` and return a RunnerResult.
00213|  *
00214|  * Auth (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, and OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA when web research is on)
00215|  * arrives via process.env — the orchestrator sets it on the `node run.mjs`
00216|  * invocation, and we pass process.env straight through to the CLI. The runner
00217|  * never handles secrets itself.
00218|  *
00219|  * @param {import('../plugin/contract.js').AgentRunInput} input
00220|  * @returns {Promise<import('../plugin/contract.js').RunnerResult>}
00221|  */
00222| export async function runAgent(input) {
00223|   const args = buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input);
00224| 
00225|   // spawnSync (not a shell string): the prompt is a plain argv element, so there
00226|   // is no shell quoting/escaping to get wrong. Blocking is fine — the runner has
00227|   // nothing else to do while the agent works. The sandbox-level timeout bounds it.
00228|   const res = spawnSync('opencode', args, {
00229|     cwd: input.cwd,
00230|     env: process.env,
00231|     encoding: 'utf8',
00232|     maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00233|   });
00234| 
00235|   const stdout = res.stdout || '';
00236|   const stderr = res.stderr || '';
00237|   // Preserve the old concatenation order: stdout THEN stderr.
00238|   const output = stdout + stderr;

00240|   const agentExitCode = res.status == null ? -1 : res.status;
00241| 
00242|   // Capture the transcript from the combined output (old: over stdout+stderr).
00243|   const transcript = extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) ?? null;
00244| 
00245|   // Resolve the model OpenCode actually used. The `--format json` events never
00246|   // include it, so first try scraping the printed logs (works on OpenCode <=
00247|   // 1.16.x), then fall back to `opencode export <sessionID>`, whose assistant
00248|   // messages carry providerID/modelID (OpenCode 1.17.0 changed the log format,
00249|   // which broke the scrape). Observation must never fail the run.
00250|   let observedModel = extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output);
00251|   if (!observedModel) {
00252|     const sessionId = extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript ?? undefined);
00253|     if (sessionId) {
00254|       try {
00255|         const exportRes = spawnSync('opencode', ['export', sessionId], {
00256|           cwd: input.cwd,
00257|           env: process.env,
00258|           encoding: 'utf8',
00259|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00260|         });

00262|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00263|         }
00264|       } catch {
00265|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00266|       }
00267|     }
00268|   }
00269|   const observedModelOrNull = normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) ?? null;
00270| 
00271|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00272|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00273|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00274|     const fallback = res.error
00275|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00276|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;
00277|     return {
00278|       ok: false,
00279|       output,
00280|       transcript,
00281|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00282|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00283|       agentExitCode,
00284|     };
00285|   }
00286| 
00287|   return {
00288|     ok: true,
00289|     output,
00290|     transcript,
00291|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00292|     error: null,
00293|     agentExitCode,
00294|   };
00295| }
00296| 
00297| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00298| 
00299| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00300| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
00301| 
00302| if (isMain) {
00303|   // argv[2] is the AgentRunInput JSON (never contains secrets).
00304|   const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
00305| 
00306|   // Always produce a RunnerResult, even if the runner itself throws, so the host
00307|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00308|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00309|   let result;
00310|   try {
00311|     result = await runAgent(input);
00312|   } catch (e) {
00313|     result = {
00314|       ok: false,
00315|       output: '',
00316|       transcript: null,
00317|       observedModel: null,
00318|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00319|       agentExitCode: -1,
00320|     };
00321|   }
00322| 
00323|   // Source of truth: the result file the host reads back via sandbox.readFile.
00324|   try {
00325|     mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });
00326|     writeFileSync(input.resultPath, JSON.stringify(result));
00327|   } catch {
00328|     // If the file can't be written, the host falls back to the marker line below.
00329|   }
00330| 
00331|   // Fallback channel: a compact status line (no transcript — it can be huge).
00332|   process.stdout.write(
00333|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00334|       JSON.stringify({
00335|         ok: result.ok,
00336|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00337|         error: result.error,
00338|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00339|       }) +
00340|       '\n'
00341|   );
00342| 
00343|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00344|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00345|   process.exit(0);
00346| }

00001| --- 00002| title: Prefetching 00003| description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js 00004| --- 00005| 00006| Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code. 00007| 00008| This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it: 00009| 00010| - [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work) 00011| - [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically) 00012| - [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching) 00013| - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) 00014| 00015| > **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path. 00016| 00017| ## How does prefetching work? 00018| 00019| When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route. 00020| 00021| Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. ---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

---
title: Prefetching
description: Learn how to configure prefetching in Next.js
---

Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

---
title: unstable_prefetch
description: API Reference for the unstable_prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation.
version: experimental
related:
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/functions/io
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
---

Calling `await unstable_prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens.

It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `unstable_prefetch()` is prerendered as usual.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

---
title: unstable_prefetch
description: API Reference for the unstable_prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation.
version: experimental
related:
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/functions/io
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
---

Calling `await unstable_prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens.

It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `unstable_prefetch()` is prerendered as usual.

## Usage

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).

00229| }
00230| 
00231| async function TeamTopics() {
00232|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00233|   return <TopicList topics={await getTopics(team)} />
00234| }
00235| 
00236| export default function Page() {
00237|   return (
00238|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00239|       <TeamTopics />
00240|     </Suspense>
00241|   )
00242| }
00243| ```
00244| 
00245| ### URL data
00246| 
00247| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00248| 
00249| ### Real-time content
00250| 
00251| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00252| 
00253| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00254| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00255| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00256| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00257| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00258| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00259| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00260| 
00261| ## Adopting incrementally
00262| 
00263| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00264| 
00265| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00266| 
00267| <FixCardGrid>
00268|   <FixCard
00269|     group="upgrade"
00270|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00271|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00272|     snippets={[
00273|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00274|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00275|     ]}
00276|   />
00277|   <FixCard
00278|     group="disable"
00279|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00280|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00281|     snippets={[
00282|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00283|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00284|       { text: '</Link>' },
00285|     ]}
00286|   />
00287| </FixCardGrid>

00289| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00290| 
00291| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00292| 
00293|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00294|    // Before
00295|    export default function Page() {
00296|      return <Dashboard />
00297|    }
00298|    ```
00299| 
00300|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00301|    // Before
00302|    export default function Page() {
00303|      return <Dashboard />
00304|    }
00305|    ```
00306| 
00307|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00308|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00309|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00310| 
00311|    export default function Page() {
00312|      return <Dashboard />
00313|    }
00314|    ```
00315| 
00316|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00317|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00318|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00319| 
00320|    export default function Page() {
00321|      return <Dashboard />
00322|    }
00323|    ```
00324| 
00325| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00326| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00327| 
00328| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:

00330| ```bash filename="Terminal"

00332| ```

00336| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00337| 
00338| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00339| 
00340| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. 00342| <FixCardGrid>
00343|   <FixCard
00344|     group="stream"
00345|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00346|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

00020| 
00021| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

00023| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00024| 
00025| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00026| 
00027| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00028| 
00029| Install the skill:
00030| 
00031| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00032| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| Then give the agent this prompt:
00036| 
00037| ```prompt
00038| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| ## Or adopt by hand
00042| 
00043| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00044| 
00045| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00046| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00047| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00048| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00049| 5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.

00051| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00052| 
00053| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00056| 
00057| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00058| 
00059| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00060| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00061| 
00062| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00063|   cacheComponents: true,
00064|   partialPrefetching: true,
00065| }
00066| 
00067| export default nextConfig
00068| ```

00070| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00071| 
00072| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00073| 
00074| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00075| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00076| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00078| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |

00080| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00081| 
00082| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00083| 
00084| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00085| 
00086| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00087| 
00088| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. 00089| 
00090| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests

00092| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. 00249| ### Real-time content

00015| ---
00016| 
00017| [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.
00018| 
00019| To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.
00020| 
00021| Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.
00022| 
00023| > **Good to know**: Partial Prefetching only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled.
00024| 
00025| ## Use the adoption skill (recommended)
00026| 
00027| The [`next-partial-prefetching-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-partial-prefetching-adoption) skill drives this adoption with a coding agent. It reviews your `<Link prefetch={true}>` calls, captures the prefetched UI to preserve with [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) when a production test rig is available, then enables the flag and checks each route for the insights this guide covers.
00028| 
00029| Install the skill:
00030| 
00031| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00032| npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-partial-prefetching-adoption
00033| ```
00034| 
00035| Then give the agent this prompt:
00036| 
00037| ```prompt
00038| Adopt Partial Prefetching in this project using the next-partial-prefetching-adoption skill.
00039| ```
00040| 
00041| ## Or adopt by hand
00042| 
00043| To adopt an existing app by hand:
00044| 
00045| 1. [Review existing full prefetches](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) and choose which part of each destination should continue to be prefetched. You can use [`instant()` tests](#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests) to add regression coverage.
00046| 2. [Enable `partialPrefetching`](#enable-partial-prefetching). For larger migrations, you can [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) with the global flag off. The [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight identifies each destination that still uses the legacy full prefetch.
00047| 3. [Move URL data behind Suspense](#move-url-data-behind-suspense), resolving the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight.
00048| 4. Optionally, [prefetch URL data](#prefetching-url-data) on the routes where streaming in after navigation isn't enough.
00049| 5. Optionally, [exclude cached content from a prefetch](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#exclude-content-from-a-prefetch) on the routes where caching content into the App Shell made it heavier than you want.
00050| 
00051| Both insights are development-only and never block the build. They appear in the dev overlay with fix cards that link the docs page for each fix. If a route isn't ready to adopt, export [`instant = false`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) from its page or layout to opt the route out of instant-navigation validation, and return to it later.
00052| 
00053| ## Enable Partial Prefetching
00054| 
00055| > **Good to know**: In an existing app, review the UI delivered by [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches) before enabling Partial Prefetching. These links use the legacy full prefetch, and enabling Partial Prefetching changes their behavior.
00056| 
00057| Enable [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) in `next.config.ts`:
00058| 
00059| ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5}
00060| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00061| 
00062| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00063|   cacheComponents: true,
00064|   partialPrefetching: true,
00065| }
00066| 
00067| export default nextConfig
00068| ```
00069| 
00070| After enabling the flag, links using the default behavior, `prefetch="auto"`, or `prefetch={true}` prefetch the destination's App Shell. A link with `prefetch={true}` can also resolve cached URL-specific content, but it no longer includes uncached dynamic content from the legacy full prefetch. New projects can enable the flag without this audit because they have no legacy full prefetches to migrate.
00071| 
00072| ## What changes for `<Link>`
00073| 
00074| | `<Link>` prop                       | Before (Cache Components default)                              | After Partial Prefetching                                                                                                                              |
00075| | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
00076| | `<Link href="/x">`                  | Prefetched the cached page render.                             | Prefetches the shared App Shell for `/x`.                                                                                                              |
00077| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch>`         | Prefetched the cached page render **and** any dynamic content. | Prefetches the App Shell, plus cached URL-specific content through [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) when `/x` reads it. |
00078| | `<Link href="/x" prefetch={false}>` | Disabled prefetching for this link.                            | Unchanged. Still disabled.                                                                                                                             |
00079| 
00080| The App Shell is shared across every link to a given route, regardless of dynamic params, so rendering many `<Link>`s to the same destination doesn't multiply the work.
00081| 
00082| ## Migrate existing full prefetches
00083| 
00084| Before Partial Prefetching, a `<Link>` whose effective `prefetch` value is `true` prefetches the complete destination, including uncached dynamic content. This includes `prefetch={true}`, the bare `prefetch` prop, and wrapper or conditional props that resolve to `true`. The default value, `prefetch="auto"`, and `prefetch={false}` don't use the legacy full prefetch.
00085| 
00086| A legacy full prefetch can include more UI than the navigation needs. In most cases, the primary content at the top of the destination should be available before navigation, while secondary or frequently changing content can stream afterward.
00087| 
00088| > **Good to know**: `cookies()` and `headers()` don't tie a prefetch to a URL. They vary per session, not per link, so the App Shell still carries session content. Only `params` and `searchParams` are [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data), which varies per link and can't be included in the shared App Shell.
00089| 
00090| ### Verify prefetched UI with tests
00091| 
00092| To verify the migration programmatically, an [`instant()`](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) test can capture the UI that should stay available from an existing full prefetch. Run this baseline against a production build with `partialPrefetching` disabled because automatic prefetching doesn't run in `next dev`. Then rerun the same assertions after adopting the destination. A failure identifies UI the App Shell no longer carries, so you can cache the data or subtree that restores it. The passing test provides regression coverage.
00093| 
00094| ### Static or cached content
00095| 
00096| The output is already in the App Shell. Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`:
00097| 
00098| ```tsx filename="app/nav.tsx"
00099| // Before
00100| <Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
00101| // After
00102| <Link href="/about">About</Link>
00103| ```
00104| 
00105| ### Uncached content
00106| 
00107| Cache it with `use cache` so it gets included in the App Shell, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00108| 
00109| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher
00110| // Before
00111| export default async function Page() {
00112|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00113|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00114| }
00115| ```
00116| 
00117| ```jsx filename="app/products/page.js" switcher

00120|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00121|   return <ProductList products={await res.json()} />
00122| }
00123| ```
00124| 
00125| ```tsx filename="app/products/page.tsx" switcher

00127| async function getProducts() {
00128|   'use cache'
00129|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00130|   return res.json()
00131| }
00132| 
00133| export default async function Page() {
00134|   return <ProductList products={await getProducts()} />
00135| }
00136| ```
00137|

00150| 
00151| > **Good to know**: The App Shell carries cached content whose [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time is at least 5 minutes, which holds for the `default` profile used above and every preset except `seconds`. Shorter-lived content streams in after the navigation instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior).
00152| 
00153| ### Session content
00154| 
00155| Content behind [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) varies per session, not per link, and [session data resolves in the App Shell](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#include-session-data-in-the-shell), so cached session content still gets included. Read the session value outside the cached function and pass it in, then remove `prefetch={true}` from the links:
00156| 
00157| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00158| // Before
00159| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00160| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00161| 
00162| async function TeamTopics() {
00163|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00164|   const topics = await db.topics.forTeam(team)
00165|   return <TopicList topics={topics} />
00166| }
00167| 
00168| export default function Page() {
00169|   return (
00170|     <Suspense fallback={<Skeleton />}>
00171|       <TeamTopics />
00172|     </Suspense>
00173|   )
00174| }
00175| ```
00176| 
00177| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher

00179| import { Suspense } from 'react'
00180| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00181| 
00182| async function TeamTopics() {
00183|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value

00191|       <TeamTopics />

00200| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00201| 
00202| async function getTopics(team: string | undefined) {
00203|   'use cache'
00204|   return db.topics.forTeam(team)
00205| }

00208|   const team = (await cookies()).get('team')?.value
00209|   return <TopicList topics={await getTopics(team)} />
00210| }

00225|

00244| 
00245| ### URL data
00246| 
00247| [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) varies per link, so content that depends on it can't be included in the shared App Shell and streams in after navigation from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary. The links keep `prefetch={true}`, and [Prefetching URL data](#prefetching-url-data) covers prefetching the content ahead of the click.
00248| 
00249| ### Real-time content
00250| 
00251| A prefetch of real-time content would be stale by the click, so there is nothing to preserve. Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in from behind its `<Suspense>` boundary.
00252| 
00253| | Destination                                                                       | Recommendation                                                            |
00254| | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
00255| | [Fully static, or content already cached](#static-or-cached-content)              | Remove the now-redundant `prefetch={true}`.                               |
00256| | [Delivered uncached content you want kept ahead of the click](#uncached-content)  | Cache it with `use cache`, then remove `prefetch={true}`.                 |
00257| | [Delivered content that depends on `cookies()` or `headers()`](#session-content)  | Cache the lookup behind the session value, then remove `prefetch={true}`. |
00258| | [Reads URL data, or has cached content that depends on it](#url-data)             | Keep `prefetch={true}` to resolve the content ahead of the click.         |
00259| | [Delivers real-time content that must stay fresh per request](#real-time-content) | Remove `prefetch={true}` and let the content stream in.                   |
00260| 
00261| ## Adopting incrementally
00262| 
00263| Adoption doesn't have to happen in one change. [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) is the global flag scoped to one route, so with the global flag still off, you can adopt and deploy each destination on its own.
00264| 
00265| Before a destination opts into Partial Prefetching, `prefetch={true}` performs the legacy full prefetch. Navigating through one of these links in development surfaces the [dynamic data during prefetching](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) insight, naming the destination and pointing at its fixes:
00266| 
00267| <FixCardGrid>
00268|   <FixCard
00269|     group="upgrade"
00270|     title="Opt into Partial Prefetching"
00271|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#opt-into-partial-prefetching"
00272|     snippets={[
00273|       { text: '// page.tsx or layout.tsx' },
00274|       { text: "export const prefetch = 'partial'", highlight: true },
00275|     ]}
00276|   />
00277|   <FixCard
00278|     group="disable"
00279|     title="Use the default prefetch"
00280|     href="/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial#use-the-default-prefetch"
00281|     snippets={[
00282|       { text: '<Link href="/dashboard">', highlight: true },
00283|       { text: '  Dashboard' },
00284|       { text: '</Link>' },
00285|     ]}
00286|   />
00287| </FixCardGrid>
00288| 
00289| Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs.
00290| 
00291| 1. Start with one destination. Preserve the intended prefetched UI and update its `prefetch={true}` links using the [patterns above](#migrate-existing-full-prefetches). Then add `export const prefetch = 'partial'` to its page or layout, which clears the insight for every link pointing at the route:
00292| 
00293|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00294|    // Before
00295|    export default function Page() {
00296|      return <Dashboard />
00297|    }
00298|    ```
00299| 
00300|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00301|    // Before
00302|    export default function Page() {
00303|      return <Dashboard />
00304|    }
00305|    ```
00306| 
00307|    ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
00308|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00309|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00310| 
00311|    export default function Page() {
00312|      return <Dashboard />
00313|    }
00314|    ```
00315| 
00316|    ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
00317|    // After - adopted without the global flag
00318|    export const prefetch = 'partial'
00319| 
00320|    export default function Page() {
00321|      return <Dashboard />
00322|    }
00323|    ```
00324| 
00325| 2. Deploy the change. Links to the adopted destination load the App Shell, and the insight keeps surfacing for the destinations you haven't reached.
00326| 3. Repeat until every destination in scope is adopted, then [enable the flag](#enable-partial-prefetching).
00327| 
00328| The per-route `prefetch = 'partial'` exports are now redundant. Remove them in one pass with the [`remove-partial-prefetch`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#remove-partial-prefetch) codemod, which strips `export const prefetch = 'partial'` from every `page` and `layout`:
00329| 
00330| ```bash filename="Terminal"
00331| npx @next/codemod@canary remove-partial-prefetch ./app
00332| ```
00333| 
00334| > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count.
00335| 
00336| The codemod removes only the `'partial'` value and leaves other values such as `prefetch = 'force-disabled'` in place.
00337| 
00338| ## Move URL data behind Suspense
00339| 
00340| With the flag enabled, Next.js validates each App Shell as you navigate in development. The App Shell is shared across every link to a route, so it can't contain data that belongs to a single URL. Reading [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional) or [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) outside a [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary ties the shell to the link's URL and surfaces the [URL data outside of Suspense](/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data) insight, naming the route and pointing at its fixes:
00341| 
00342| <FixCardGrid>
00343|   <FixCard
00344|     group="stream"
00345|     title="Wrap in or move into Suspense"
00346|     href="/docs/messages/instant-shell-url-data#wrap-in-or-move-into-suspense"

00376|     </ProductLayout>
00377|   )
00378| }
00379| ```
00380|

00389|     </ProductLayout>
00390|   )
00391| }

00397| import { ProductDetails } from './product-details'
00398| 
00399| export default function Page({ params }: PageProps<'/products/[slug]'>) {

00409| 
00410| ```jsx filename="app/products/[slug]/page.js" switcher

00414|

00417|     <ProductLayout>
00418|       <Suspense fallback={<DetailsSkeleton />}>

00450| ## Prefetching URL data
00451| 
00452| Content that depends on [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) (`params`, `searchParams`) can't be included in the shared App Shell, so it streams in after navigation. title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
nav_title: Adopting Partial Prefetching
description: Learn how to enable Partial Prefetching and what changes for `<Link>`.
related:
  title: Next Steps
  description: Learn more about prefetching and instant navigations.
  links:
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching

    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
---

[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

title: Optimizing prefetching
description: Resolve per-link URL data with the prefetch prop, include session data in the App Shell, or exclude expensive content from a prefetch.
nav_title: Optimizing prefetching
related:
  title: Learn more
  description: Validate your structure and review the caching primitives.
  links:
    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching
    - app/api-reference/functions/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/functions/navigation
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
    - app/getting-started/caching
    - app/guides/instant-navigation
    - app/guides/prefetching
---

Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
